newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Pemex sees crude, gas output rising in 97. [CORRECTED 19:44 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Pemex sees crude, gas output rising in 97. [CORRECTED 19:44 GMT]

text.p: Mexico's state-owned oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) sees crude and natural gas output rising in 1997 over forecast levels for 1996, a company manager said Thursday.

Alberto Imaz, manager of operational planning of Pemex's exploration and production unit, said crude production would rise 8 percent next year from the output expected this year of 2.86 million barrels per day (bpd).

Imaz, speaking at a steel conference here in Mexico's western city, said natural gas output would rise 6 percent next year from the 4.19 (corrects figure from 4.9) million cubic feet per day (cfd) forecast for 1996.
